report_name: Water Hydra's DarkMe RAT Campaign Pivots to Phishing Attacks

threat_actors.name: Water Hydra
threat_actors.description: A financially motivated APT group that has shifted tactics from using zero-day exploits to simple phishing attacks to distribute the DarkMe RAT. The group is broadening its target base beyond the financial sector.

attack_patterns.name: Spearphishing Link
attack_patterns.description: The attack chain begins with a phishing email containing a lure, such as a fake image link, which when clicked downloads the initial malicious .pif payload.

attack_patterns.name: User Execution: Malicious File
attack_patterns.description: A user is required to execute a downloaded Program Information File (.pif), which is an executable disguised as a shortcut, to initiate the infection.

attack_patterns.name: System Checks
attack_patterns.description: The DarkMe loader performs an inverted sandbox check by verifying the presence of 329 common user applications (e.g., Slack, Zoom). If none are found, it assumes it is in a sandbox and terminates.

attack_patterns.name: Process Hollowing
attack_patterns.description: The final DarkMe RAT payload is injected into the memory of a legitimate, Microsoft-signed process, clspack.exe, to evade detection.

attack_patterns.name: Component Object Model Hijacking
attack_patterns.description: The malware achieves persistence by registering a custom COM object to ensure it is re-executed.

attack_patterns.name: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
attack_patterns.description: The malware creates a `Locked://` URI protocol handler in the Windows Registry to achieve persistence.

attack_patterns.name: Non-Application Layer Protocol
attack_patterns.description: The DarkMe RAT communicates with its command and control server using a custom TCP protocol on port 7712.

malware.name: DarkMe
malware.description: A Remote Access Trojan (RAT) distributed by the Water Hydra group. It is delivered via a multi-stage VB6 loader and uses process hollowing for evasion. Its capabilities include stealing cryptocurrency wallets, capturing screenshots, logging keystrokes, and providing remote access.

vulnerabilities.name: CVE-2023-38831
vulnerabilities.description: A WinRAR flaw that was previously used by the Water Hydra group in past campaigns before they pivoted to phishing for DarkMe distribution.

infrastructure.name: DarkMe C2 Infrastructure
infrastructure.description: Command and control infrastructure used by the DarkMe RAT, communicating over a custom TCP protocol on port 7712.

indicators.name: DarkMe RAT C2 Network Connection
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: DarkMe RAT C2 Connection
id: 7c8b1a2d-3e4f-4a5b-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d
status: experimental
description: Detects network connections to known DarkMe RAT C2 infrastructure on port 7712.
references:
  - https://www.huntress.com/blog/darkme-rat-abandons-exploits
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-23
tags:
  - attack.t1095
  - attack.command_and_control
level: critical
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_ip:
    DestinationIp: '67.43.50.11'
    DestinationPort: 7712
    Initiated: 'true'
  selection_dns:
    DestinationHostname: 'thatawful.boutique'
    DestinationPort: 7712
    Initiated: 'true'
  condition: 1 of them
indicators.description: Detects outbound network traffic to the DarkMe RAT C2 domain or IP address on the specific C2 port 7712.

indicators.name: DarkMe Process Hollowing of clspack.exe
indicators.pattern:
title: DarkMe RAT Process Hollowing of clspack.exe
id: 8d9e0f1a-2b3c-4d5e-8f9a-0b1c2d3e4f5a
status: experimental
description: Detects the legitimate process clspack.exe making unexpected outbound network connections, a behavior associated with DarkMe RAT process hollowing.
references:
  - https://www.huntress.com/blog/darkme-rat-abandons-exploits
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-23
tags:
  - attack.t1055.012
  - attack.defense_evasion
level: high
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\clspack.exe'
    Initiated: 'true'
  filter_local:
    DestinationIp|cidr:
      - '127.0.0.0/8'
      - '::1/128'
  condition: selection and not filter_local
indicators.description: Detects the legitimate Windows process `clspack.exe` making outbound network connections, which is anomalous and indicative of the process hollowing technique used by DarkMe.

indicators.name: DarkMe Persistence via URI Protocol Handler
indicators.pattern:
title: DarkMe RAT Persistence via URI Protocol Handler
id: 9e0f1a2b-3c4d-4e5f-9a0b-1c2d3e4f5a6b
status: experimental
description: Detects the creation of a 'Locked://' URI protocol handler in the registry, a persistence technique used by DarkMe RAT.
references:
  - https://www.huntress.com/blog/darkme-rat-abandons-exploits
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-23
tags:
  - attack.t1546.015
  - attack.t1547.001
  - attack.persistence
level: high
logsource:
  category: registry_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetObject|startswith: 'HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\Locked'
    EventType: 'CreateKey'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the creation of the `HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\Locked` registry key, which establishes a custom URI protocol handler for persistence as used by DarkMe.

indicators.name: Execution of PIF File
indicators.pattern:
title: Execution of PIF File
id: a0b1c2d3-e4f5-4a6b-8c7d-8e9f0a1b2c3d
status: experimental
description: Detects the execution of a Program Information File (.pif), which is often used to disguise executables in phishing campaigns like the one delivering DarkMe RAT.
references:
  - https://www.huntress.com/blog/darkme-rat-abandons-exploits
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-23
tags:
  - attack.t1204.002
  - attack.execution
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '.pif'
    OriginalFileName|endswith: '.pif'
  condition: 1 of selection
indicators.description: Detects the execution of a `.pif` file, a technique used in this campaign for initial execution of the malware loader.
